claims.text: Atom Probe Tomography with optimized sample preparation can analyze nanoprecipitate interfaces in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 produced by additive manufacturing.
High-temperature oxidation induces near-atomic-scale elemental segregation at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Interfacial elemental segregation correlates with the formation of protective oxide phases.
The protective oxide phases enhance oxidation resistance.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains well-dispersed nanoprecipitates in a high-entropy matrix.
Nanoprecipitate interfaces act as the relevant structural mediator during oxidation.
Oxidation drives selective elemental diffusion in the alloy.
Titanium and chromium may segregate at nanoprecipitate interfaces during oxidation.
Segregation at nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitates the nucleation and growth of protective oxide phases.
APT can be used to obtain three-dimensional elemental concentration maps across nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
The oxidized sample will exhibit measurable enrichment of key elements at nanoprecipitate interfaces relative to the unoxidized baseline.
Interfacial enrichment will correlate with improved oxidation resistance.
Sample-preparation artifacts or APT resolution limits may affect measurements in regions with sharp composition gradients.
The extent and elemental identity of the redistribution may vary with small composition or processing changes.
